name: White Rabbit
timbre: thin, reedy, slightly nasal older man's voice, breathy and fluttering, with a sharp edge when giving orders
pitch: high tenor for an older man, jumpy intonation that climbs when panicked
accent: genteel southern English, affected Received Pronunciation of an upper servant, clipped and fussy
reference_style: Two voices from one throat: breathless, stammering and servile upward (Duchess, Queen, King); peremptory and snappish downward (Mary Ann, Pat, Bill). As trial herald he reads out 'at the top of his shrill little voice'. Animal oaths ('my ears and whiskers') are spoken as nervous tics.

panicked.note: 'Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!' — breathy, overlapping gasps

ordering_down.note: ch004-p02 'in an angry tone' — shrill snap

servile_low.note: ch008-p36 'in a low, hurried tone'; ch011-p67 'in a low voice'

herald_proclaim.note: ch011-p74 'at the top of his shrill little voice' — formal, thin, strained

voice_evidence.quote: the White Rabbit read out, at the top of his shrill little voice
said a timid voice at her side
said the Rabbit in a low, hurried tone

reason: 'Shrill little voice' and timid/hurried tones are sourced; pitch band, rate and accent designed for an anxious 1862 upper servant (dialogue_style register).
